A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LCPO research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original grid-world, wind-driven Gymnasium, and straggler-mitigation experiments, including comparative results and ablations in Section 6 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds comparator results, OOD experiments, an LCPO-P comparison, and computational measurements in Section 5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The principal constrained LCPO algorithm is retained. Appendix E.1 introduces LCPO-P, an alternative that uses a cross-entropy anchoring penalty and repeated PPO updates instead of LCPO's hard anchoring constraint.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same grid-world example, five Gymnasium environments under four wind traces, and straggler mitigation on two production workloads. The added OOD and LCPO-P studies vary detector or optimizer configurations within this coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Tables 5–6 add evaluated Sliding OGD, CLEAR, BFDQN, and PT-DQN comparators. Appendix E.1 also compares LCPO-P. The buffer-size table replaces individually listed baseline columns with the best baseline per condition; the oracle-to-prescient renaming does not introduce a new comparator.

E3.justification: The grid-world diagnostic changes from up-action probability for one context to total-variation distance for both contexts. Added experiments specify OOD metric/threshold configurations and PPO settings for LCPO-P. Existing action discretization and main LCPO hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: OOD sensitivity testing expands beyond the retained straggler thresholds to Gymnasium threshold sweeps and a detector using joint state-context inputs without their separation. New analyses compare constrained anchoring with LCPO-P and examine forgetting in both grid-world modes. Existing buffer-size and ideal-model MBPO checks remain.

E5.justification: v3 reports 25 seeds for most main Gymnasium comparisons instead of five, retaining five for MBPO/MBCD and ten for straggler experiments. CDFs gain 95% confidence bands, and table captions explicitly define boldface through 95%-confidence superiority. Confidence intervals already existed in v2's tables.

E6.justification: Many Gymnasium estimates change alongside revised seed counts: LCPO on Pendulum trace 2 changes from -357 ±6.38 to -355 ±2.57. New comparator, OOD, LCPO-P, and runtime results substantially expand the evidence. Straggler Table 1 remains numerically unchanged; updated estimates do not establish an algorithmic performance gain.

T1.justification: v3 adds formal lifelong-average-return definitions, Lemma B.1 and Theorem B.2 with a tabular Q-learning convergence proof under restricted context assumptions, and binomial OOD-sampling analysis. These are absent from v2. The theorem's printed reward and learning-rate inequalities contain apparent sign errors.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains OOD-based policy anchoring to mitigate forgetting without task labels in observed exogenous-context environments. Both versions claim strong aggregate performance relative to online baselines and proximity to offline-trained policies. Expanded supporting evidence and oracle-to-prescient terminology do not redefine that contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations for Sliding OGD, CLEAR, and PT-DQN failures and for LCPO-P's sensitivity to its penalty coefficient. It develops the causal-versus-prescient performance distinction, discusses OOD tuning requirements, and proposes forgetting sufficiently old contexts when network capacity becomes limiting.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds reservoir and OOD-sampling pseudocode and implementation detail. v3 also supplies new baseline/LCPO-P hyperparameters, warm-up details, software versions/licenses, and runtime information, and changes the code-access pointer. It newly discloses that the straggler environment and dataset are nonpublic and proprietary.

R1.justification: Section 3 and new Appendix A substantially expand positioning against latent-context inference, meta-learning, multitask RL, stationary interference, and limited-buffer methods. New citations include Woo et al. (2022) and Anand and Precup (2023), with detailed discussion of how their approaches differ from LCPO.

P1.justification: v3 reorganizes the illustration and methodology into subsections, moves detailed baseline explanations into Appendix D, rewrites the related-work narrative, and reverses the ordering of the two sensitivity sections. It adopts prescient terminology, adds reproducibility and acknowledgement sections, and removes the generic broader-impact section.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation. v3 merges and expands the grid-world figures, adds an LCPO architecture diagram and new analysis tables, splits the main benchmark table, and rearranges existing context and latency panels. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v2's limited continual-learning comparator coverage and evidence for the anchoring design through additional baselines, Gymnasium OOD tests, and the LCPO-P comparison. More reported seeds, computational measurements, and implementation details strengthen empirical reliability and transparency. The new theorem's erroneous printed inequalities require correction, but this localized weakness does not outweigh the substantial validation and documentation gains.
